label: Persistent Identifier
description: Does your service assign persistent identifiers to datasets?
definition: Persistent identifiers (PIDs) uniquely and permanently identify digital objects, enabling reliable tracking and access to datasets over time.

label: Rich Metadata
description: Does your service provide rich metadata?
definition: Rich metadata includes comprehensive descriptive, structural, and administrative information about data, facilitating discovery and reusability.

label: Indexed In Search Engines
description: Is your metadata indexed in major search engines?
definition: Metadata indexing in search engines ensures that datasets are discoverable through standard web search tools and data discovery services.

label: Metadata Schema
description: Does your database use formal or standard metadata schemas?
definition: Standard metadata schemas provide structured formats for describing data, enabling interoperability and consistent interpretation across systems.

label: Metadata Persistence
description: Is your metadata persistently available over time?
definition: Metadata persistence ensures that descriptive information about datasets remains accessible and unchanged throughout the data lifecycle.

label: Retrieval Protocol
description: Is there a standard protocol available for data retrieval?
definition: Standard retrieval protocols (e.g., HTTP, FTP, OAI-PMH) enable reliable and predictable access to data using established technical standards.

label: Authentication Required
description: Does your database require authentication for data access?
definition: Authentication mechanisms verify user identity before granting access to data, supporting both open and restricted access scenarios.

label: Authentication Type
description: If yes, what type of authentication is used?
definition: Different authentication types (e.g., username/password, OAuth, certificates) provide varying levels of security and usability for data access.

label: Metadata Always Available
description: Is metadata always accessible, even if the data is restricted?
definition: Metadata availability independent of data access allows discovery and understanding of restricted datasets, supporting transparency and informed decisions.

label: Data Availability
description: Is the actual data accessible (open or controlled access)?
definition: Data availability ensures that datasets are retrievable through documented, standardized access mechanisms supporting both open and controlled access policies.

label: Knowledge Representation
description: Do you use formal knowledge representation (e.g., ontologies, RDF)?
definition: Formal knowledge representation using ontologies and semantic languages enables machine-interpretable descriptions of data relationships and meanings.

label: Vocabularies Used
description: Do you enforce the use of controlled vocabularies for data submission?
definition: Controlled vocabularies and standard terminologies ensure consistent representation of concepts, improving data integration and semantic interoperability.

label: Qualified References
description: Do you validate and qualify references (e.g., external IDs) before data submission?
definition: Qualified references with resolvable identifiers enable linking between datasets and external resources, enhancing data connectivity and context.

label: Api Availability
description: Do you provide a dedicated API for data access?
definition: Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) provide programmatic access to data, enabling automated integration with other systems and workflows.

label: Data Formats
description: Do you use standardized data formats in your database or API?
definition: Standardized, non-proprietary data formats ensure data portability and compatibility across different tools and systems.

label: License Clarity
description: Does your database clearly state licenses for data reuse?
definition: Clear licensing information informs users about permitted uses, modifications, and redistribution of data, supporting legal compliance and responsible reuse.

label: Provenance Info
description: Do you provide provenance information?
definition: Provenance documentation tracks the origin, processing history, and transformations applied to data, supporting validation and trustworthiness assessment.

label: Community Standards
description: Do your data formats adhere to community standards?
definition: Community-adopted standards ensure data compatibility within research domains and facilitate domain-specific tool integration and reuse.

label: Documentation Quality
description: Do you provide documentation for using your database?
definition: Comprehensive documentation enables users to understand data structure, methodology, limitations, and proper usage for accurate interpretation and reuse.

label: Citation Guidelines
description: Have you clearly stated citation guidelines?
definition: Clear citation guidelines ensure proper attribution and reproducibility, supporting research integrity and acknowledgment of data contributions.
